solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Shrub’s rating in puzzle — hard! (8)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing inside another, so the rating is set within the puzzle

blocks.note: OS = ordinary seaman, a naval rating
a rebus is a picture puzzle; OS goes in after its R
H = hard, as on pencils

annotation.surface: Someone grumbles that a shrub earns a hard score in a puzzle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rating' looks like a score but is a sailor: OS, ordinary seaman. The 's is a link: the shrub 'is' what the wordplay builds.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain relation of kind: a rose is a shrub, and the whole plant is the bush.

entries.clue: Little bridge support collecting river plant (6,4)

indicatorNotes.collecting: to collect something is to gather it in, so the support holds the river inside it

blocks.note: a rubber is a short set of games at bridge
a tee supports a golf ball
R = river, inside TEE

annotation.surface: A small bridge has a support that has caught a river plant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' is the card game, not a span over water; a rubber is a best-of-three set of its games.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the rubber tree, tapped for latex and grown as a houseplant, is a plant.

entries.clue: Magistrates crime detectives listened to (7)

indicatorNotes.listened to: what is listened to is heard, so the words count for their sound rather than their spelling

blocks.note: sin = crime; dicks = detectives, US slang

annotation.surface: Magistrates listened to what the police investigators had to say.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dick' is old American slang for a private detective. A syndic is a civic official or magistrate in some countries.
annotation.definitionFit: Historical sense: syndics were magistrates or chief officials in various European cities, such as Geneva.

entries.clue: Warcraft one team rowed with another over (6)

annotation.definition: Warcraft one team rowed with another over

blocks.note: reads like the name of a video game; it is simply a craft built for war

blocks.clueFragment: one team rowed with another over
blocks.note: sounds like one crew quarrelling with another; really two tiers of oarsmen, one sitting above the other

annotation.surface: A warship where one rowing crew sat over another.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Over' reads like the end of a quarrel between teams; it means one deck of oarsmen sat above the other, which is what a bireme is.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes an ancient galley with two banks of oars, the second bank above the first.

entries.clue: Unaffected by wicked magic (12)

blocks.note: wicked = excellent in slang, i.e. super
unaffected = natural, without airs

annotation.surface: Something is untouched by evil spells.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' pairs with 'magic' to suggest witchcraft, but it is the slang praise word. 'By' only places the pieces side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: Adjective for adjective: magic powers are supernatural, beyond the laws of nature.

entries.clue: Show boldly cut to accommodate piano (6)

indicatorNotes.to accommodate: to accommodate is to make room for, so the cut takes the piano inside it

blocks.note: slash = cut
p = piano, soft in music; it sits inside SLASH

annotation.surface: A bold cut is made to fit a piano into a room.
annotation.walkthrough: To splash a story is to display it prominently, as a newspaper does on its front page.
annotation.definitionFit: Journalistic sense: a paper that splashes a story shows it boldly across the front page.

entries.clue: Shop quick to stifle abuse (8)

indicatorNotes.to stifle: to stifle is to smother, so quick closes all round abuse

blocks.note: pacy = quick
harm = abuse; it goes inside PACY

annotation.surface: A plea to report a shop quickly to put a stop to abuse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Quick' reads as an adverb urging someone to act fast; it is an adjective, and the shop at the front is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: in Britain a pharmacy is the chemist's, the shop that dispenses medicines.

entries.clue: Port in a new mug (7)

blocks.note: as printed
N = new
a mug is a fool, a twerp

annotation.surface: Port wine served in a fresh mug.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Port' and 'mug' suggest a drink in a cup; port is the harbour and a mug is a gullible fool in British slang.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: Antwerp is one of Europe's largest seaports, in Belgium.

entries.clue: Rush out of capital city, avoiding the centre (4)

indicatorNotes.out of: 'out of' says the answer is made from the material that follows
indicatorNotes.avoiding the centre: to avoid the centre is to steer round the middle, so the city's middle letters are left out

blocks.note: Harare, capital of Zimbabwe
the city has six letters, so its centre is the third and fourth; those two go

annotation.surface: An urge to flee a capital, keeping clear of its downtown.
annotation.walkthrough: Taking RA from the middle of HARARE leaves the verb for running fast.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, informal: to hare is to rush, running off as fast as a hare.

entries.clue: Intricate prank, but ruined (8)

indicatorNotes.Intricate: something intricate is intertwined and complex, so the letters are tangled into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: An elaborate practical joke that nonetheless came to nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ruined' looks like a comment on the prank; it is the definition, in the money sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the financial sense: a bankrupt business is ruined, unable to pay its debts.

entries.clue: Parrot fancier’s hobby? (6)

annotation.definitionNote: definition by example: a hobby is one kind of raptor, flagged by the question mark

indicatorNotes.fancier: fancier means more elaborate or ornamented, so the word is dressed up in a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A bird-lover's pastime is keeping parrots.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fancier' is a bird fancier and 'hobby' a pastime; a hobby is really a small falcon, so the question mark flags a bird of prey given by example.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the hobby is a small falcon, and falcons are birds of prey.

entries.clue: Measurement by part of the UK Met Office (8,4)

blocks.note: one of the UK's four nations
a yard is a measure of length, three feet

annotation.surface: A weather reading taken by the Met Office in one region of Britain.
annotation.walkthrough: The Met Office is the UK weather service; here 'Met' is the Metropolitan Police, London's force.
annotation.definitionFit: Metonym: the Metropolitan Police headquarters has long been known by the name of its original street, so it is the Met's office.

entries.clue: Before a town crier almost replaced a comedian (4,9)

indicatorNotes.Before: 'before' means ahead of, so the rearranged crier comes in front of the town
indicatorNotes.almost: almost means not quite all, so crier loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.replaced: to replace is to put back in a new place, so the remaining letters are reordered

blocks.note: CRIER minus its last R is CRIE, rearranged
Morecambe, a seaside town in Lancashire

annotation.surface: Before a town crier was replaced, a comedian nearly did the job.
annotation.walkthrough: The comedian took his stage name from his home town in Lancashire, which is why 'a town' can stand for his surname.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: Eric Morecambe, of the double act Morecambe and Wise, was one of Britain's best-loved comedians.

entries.clue: Sadly ego stops scientists surveying (10)

indicatorNotes.Sadly: sadly can mean badly or deplorably, so ego is treated badly and its letters jumbled

blocks.note: EGO rearranged
desists = stops

annotation.surface: Regrettably, vanity halts researchers doing survey work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stops' looks like the verb acting on scientists; it is simply the second piece, tacked on after the rearranged ego.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: geodesy is the science of surveying and measuring the Earth's shape.

entries.clue: International pilot (4)

blocks.note: a match between national sides, in cricket or rugby the formal full kind
a pilot is a trial run of a scheme or programme

annotation.surface: An airline pilot who flies internationally.
annotation.walkthrough: Both words look like aviation; a Test match is a full international fixture in cricket or rugby, and a pilot is a trial.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a Test is an international match, and a pilot study is a test of an idea.

entries.clue: Ending for one piece about intellectual property (10)

annotation.definitionNote: definition by example: 'ending' is one participle

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so the piece goes round the property

blocks.note: a particle is a tiny piece
IP = intellectual property; it sits inside PARTIC…LE

annotation.surface: A closing note on a written piece about copyright.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ending' reads as a noun, a conclusion; it is the word 'ending' itself, and 'for one' says it is an example of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: 'ending' is the present participle of the verb 'end'.

entries.clue: Wine? Enter a US alternative! (8)

indicatorNotes.alternative: an alternative is another option, so the letters take another arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A wine list offering an American substitute.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is usually spelt with a final S; the S-less form is the anglicised or American spelling.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: it is a sweet white dessert wine from Bordeaux.

entries.clue: Off course old vehicle has river to follow (10)

indicatorNotes.to follow: to follow is to come after, so the river goes behind the old vehicle

blocks.note: ex = former
a tram is a vehicle
the Ural, a Russian river

annotation.surface: An old vehicle has gone off course and a river lies ahead of it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Off course' suggests going astray; here it means outside the university's regular courses.
annotation.definitionFit: Academic sense: extramural study happens outside a university's walls, off its regular course.

entries.clue: Disaster of old in loveless old city (7)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing inside another, so AGED is set within what is left of the city
indicatorNotes.loveless: love is zero in tennis, so loveless means the city loses its O

blocks.note: ancient Troy
remove O from TROY
aged = old; it goes inside TR…Y

annotation.surface: A long-ago catastrophe in a city without love.
annotation.walkthrough: The first 'old' is AGED; the second belongs with 'city' and points to ancient Troy, fitting the Greek-drama feel of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a tragedy is a disaster or calamity.

entries.clue: After retiring finally settled on Lincoln (4)

indicatorNotes.finally: finally means at the end, so take the last letter of settled
indicatorNotes.on: in an across entry 'on' means placed after, so that letter follows Lincoln

blocks.note: Abe Lincoln, US president
last letter of settleD

annotation.surface: After retirement someone finally made a home in Lincoln.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' means going to bed, not leaving work; Lincoln is the president, not the English city.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: to retire is to go to bed for the night, so afterwards you lie in bed.

entries.clue: Puzzles sound diverting devices (7)

blocks.note: to puzzle is to bewilder or perplex
panels or plates that deflect sound, as in a loudspeaker cabinet

annotation.surface: Puzzles that are genuinely entertaining gadgets.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sound diverting' reads as 'truly amusing'; it means devices that divert sound.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a verb meaning perplexes, and a noun for boards that deflect sound or flow.

entries.clue: Runner in decline, not entirely careful (6)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing inside another, so the runner sits within the decline
indicatorNotes.not entirely: not entirely means not all of it, so decline loses its last letter

blocks.note: fall = decline
FALL minus its last letter
a runner is a long narrow rug; it goes inside FA…L

annotation.surface: An athlete in decline is not quite as careful as before.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete; it is the long strip of carpet laid in a hall.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the money sense: someone careful with spending is thrifty and sparing.

entries.clue: Old style darts can bust water vessels (4,3,6)

indicatorNotes.bust: something bust is broken, so the letters of darts can are smashed and reassembled

blocks.note: DARTS CAN rearranged
rafts are vessels on water

annotation.surface: Old-fashioned darts can smash water jugs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Water vessels' suggests jugs; they are boats. The answer is the late-Victorian design movement led by William Morris.
annotation.definitionFit: Historical sense: the name belongs to a nineteenth-century decorative style, so it is an old style.

entries.clue: Plots showing up in emails, regularly filtered (4)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition describes what spam is: the stuff in emails that is routinely filtered

indicatorNotes.showing up: in a down entry, 'up' means read from bottom to top, so the word turns round

blocks.note: to plot a course is to map it; plots and maps are both charts

annotation.surface: Schemes turning up in emails keep getting filtered out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' tempts you to take alternate letters of 'emails'; that gives EAL or MIS. Here it just means routinely.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: junk mail is what inbox filters routinely catch.

entries.clue: Essay by a writer of tales in verse (6)

blocks.note: Edgar Allan Poe, author of Tales of Mystery and Imagination
an essay is an attempt, a try

annotation.surface: An essay by a storyteller, written in rhyme.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Essay' means an attempt, not a composition, and the writer's pieces come in the reverse of clue order.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: verse and poetry both mean writing arranged in metrical lines.

entries.clue: Fruit fly brought back only from the east (8)

indicatorNotes.brought back: something brought back returns the way it came, so the fly is read backwards
indicatorNotes.from the east: an across entry normally reads west to east; read from the east, the word runs right to left

blocks.note: a gnat is a small fly
sole = only

annotation.surface: Fruit flies were brought in exclusively from Asia.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fruit fly' is a false phrase: 'Fruit' is the definition and 'fly' is the insect in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a tangelo is a citrus fruit, a cross of tangerine and pomelo.

entries.clue: PM forced out by border chaos (6)

blocks.note: Theresa May, UK prime minister forced out in 2019
a hem is the border of cloth

annotation.surface: A prime minister ousted amid chaos at the border.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Border' suggests frontier politics; it is the edge of a garment. Theresa May resigned as British prime minister in 2019 under pressure from her party.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: violent disorder and confusion, the state the surface describes in Westminster.

entries.clue: Does Love Island featuring oldies for a change (8)

indicatorNotes.featuring: to feature something is to include it, so the island holds the changed oldies
indicatorNotes.for a change: doing something 'for a change' means doing it differently, so the letters of oldies take a different order

blocks.note: IS = island, on maps
OLDIES rearranged, placed inside I…S

annotation.surface: An older cast appears on the reality show Love Island as a novelty.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue borrows Love Island, a British TV dating show; the definition is the first two words, with 'does' as an emphatic.
annotation.definitionFit: Emphatic verb: someone who really does love another worships them.
